messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Increased tail latency observed for streaming endpoints (/v1/stream/*) in us-west-2. 95th latency trending > 1.2s for last 6m, error rate up ~0.5%. Triggering paging workflow.

pagerduty: Paging Emily Chen (oncall). Please ack and triage.

Emily Chen: Acked. Jumping in — looking at mux metrics now.

Emily Chen: Seeing persistent increase in mux queue depth on gpu-pool-3, bursts coincide with a spike in long-lived streams. CPU on the mux hosts also high.

Sanjay Patel: Are these new model rollouts or heavy prompt patterns?

Emily Chen: No rollout in last 3 hours per deploy-bot, traffic shape change — a handful of clients ramping long streaming sessions.

Liam Wong: If streams are staying open, they prevent batching and increase tail latency. We should consider a temporary mitigation: move streaming traffic to non-streaming fallback or reduce streaming concurrency.

Mina Hsu: +1. Prepare to flip quiet-mode for streaming: disable chunked SSE and return non-streaming final responses for a short window. Minimal code path change on router.

Ops-bot: Proposed mitigation plan:
1) Rate-limit new streaming starts to 10r/s per region.
2) Toggle streaming feature flag to "quiet-mode" returning final JSON payloads immediately (no SSE frames).
3) Shift quotas from streaming to non-streaming routes to preserve client quotas.
Action window: 30 minutes, reassess.

Emily Chen: I like 2 + 3. Rate-limits alone may cause retry storms. We'll do both.

Sanjay Patel: Who can flip the feature flag? I can if someone approves.

Ryan K: I will bless the change. Ops, go ahead. Post the curl you will run.

Mina Hsu: Running the admin toggle from runbook. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/feature-flags/streaming-mode \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode":"quiet","reason":"latency-mitigation","expires_at":"2026-03-15T11:05:00Z"}'
```

Mina Hsu: Also updating rate-limiter:
```
shardctl set-rate --shard us-west-2 --route "/v1/stream/*" --limit 10r/s --burst 20 --comment "mitigation 2799990001"
```

Emily Chen: I'm going to patch routing rules to send streaming-capable clients to /v1/generate (non-stream) when the feature flag is quiet. Adding a fallback header so SDKs can detect and switch.

deploy-bot: No deploys detected in last 3h. Safe to toggle runtime flags.

Mina Hsu: Executing flag toggle now.

Ops-bot: Toggle applied: streaming-mode=quiet in us-west-2 (response OK). Changed rate limits on stream route.

Emily Chen: Observability — immediate: mux queue depth dropping, CPU usage down 30% on mux hosts. 95th latency for non-stream endpoints stable.

Sanjay Patel: Quick question — customer impact? Which clients see different behavior?

Emily Chen: Only streaming sessions initiated after the toggle get quiet-mode. Existing open streams are left to drain (we set short keepalive so they close soon). Rough estimate: ~1.2% of live requests are streaming starts; most will get a single final response instead of streamed frames. Expect function-calling SDKs to still work but with a single aggregated response.

Mina Hsu: Notifying front-line support and product: sending canned blurb to #support.

Emily Chen: Posting incident blurb to status page internal: short-lived streaming fallback deployed to preserve latency and quota.

Liam Wong: Any observed retry storms? Logs show small spike of client reconnect attempts; throttling prevented overload.

Ryan K: Good. How long are we planning to keep quiet-mode?

Emily Chen: Initial window 30 minutes. If metrics normal, we'll revert. If still high, extend and start targeted throttles by client.

Sanjay Patel: Can we push notification to SDKs about fallback so they can gracefully degrade?

Mina Hsu: Added response header X-Redwood-Streaming-Fallback: quiet-mode. I'll add a short note to developer status and SDKs to watch header.

Ops-bot: Updated quotas: shifted 5% of streaming quota pool to non-streaming buckets for 30m.

Emily Chen: Customer-impact assessment: based on telemetry, ~0.4% of paying customers may observe reduced streaming UX (no incremental frames) during mitigation. No errors introduced, only different delivery mode. Major customers with contractual streaming SLAs: contacting account teams now.

Sanjay Patel: Thanks. @Emily please hit the postmortem owner button once we stabilize.

Emily Chen: Will create a follow-up ticket with root-cause hypothesis (client behavior causing long-lived streams) and mitigation runbook updates. Tentative owner: Emily + Sanjay.

Mina Hsu: Metrics now: 95th latency on router dropped from 1.2s -> 650ms within 90s of toggle. Error rate back to baseline.

Liam Wong: Nice. Recommend keeping quiet-mode for 20 more minutes to confirm.

Emily Chen: Extending window to 50 minutes total; expire at 2026-03-15T11:25:00Z.

Ops-bot: Updated expires_at for feature flag.

Emily Chen: Will start staged revert at +50m if stable: revert flag, remove rate limits, revert quotas. Revert will be staged across 5 minutes.

Ryan K: Approving staged revert plan. Notify in this thread before final revert.

Emily Chen: Noted. Monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-mitigation?panel=overview

Mina Hsu: Heads-up to support: short template sent to private support channel for customer comms.

Emily Chen: Keeping this thread open. Will update on revert or if we need further escalation.

Ops-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation applied successfully.

Emily Chen: Follow-up at 2799990060: small regression in client-side timeouts observed; ops already adjusted client keepalive guidance in SDK docs (internal patch).

Sanjay Patel: Good catch. Make sure we include guidance in postmortem.

Emily Chen: Last update 2799990099: Metrics stable for 25 minutes; preparing staged revert in 10m unless something changes.

Liam Wong: Thanks everyone — nice runbook execution.

Emily Chen: Reassigning postmortem to Emily + Sanjay. Closing this mitigation thread after revert.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged closed for active paging.

Emily Chen: Reverting feature flag now (scheduled staggered revert). Will post final status after completion.

Ops-bot: Revert completed. Streaming restored in us-west-2, rate-limits removed, quotas returned.

Emily Chen: Final: router 95th latency stable ~420ms, error rates normal. Postmortem ticket: RWF-INC-279999.

Mina Hsu: Added runbook note: add auto-detect for unusually long stream durations and proactive throttles.

Emily Chen: Thanks team. Follow-up actions in ticket.
